final_answer:
PRIVILEGED - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
TO: Kate Ellsworth | FROM: Litigation team | RE: Hargrove v. Commissioner, No. 8341-23 - analysis of Respondent's 12/6/2024 markup of our 11/1/2024 proposed Stipulation (Rule 91)

1. BOTTOM LINE
Do not sign or accept the markup as a redline. It does not match what we served, understates and mislabels changes, and includes factual substitutions contradicted by our documents. Reject six items outright, negotiate four, accept the housekeeping. Our own draft also contains errors that must be fixed before we can credibly demand accuracy. Key dates: IRS call offered 12/17-19; stipulation deadline 1/15/2025; Rule 91(f) motion window closes 2/28/2025 (45 days before 4/14 calendar call); trial 4/14/2025.

2. THRESHOLD PROBLEM: THE MARKUP IS NOT A TRUE REDLINE
- Cover letter claims 34 modified, 8 deleted, 12 added paragraphs. The markup's own index shows 12 substantive edits (22, 38, 47, 78, 83, 89-93, 112, 139), 3 typo fixes, 3 EIN additions, 5 deleted paragraphs (62-65, 118) and 12 additions (148-159). Roughly 19-22 modifications and 3 deletions are unaccounted for.
- Numbering and content differ from our served draft throughout (ours: 62-65 are the IC memorandum, board minutes and Feb. 2018 minutes; ours ends at 147 with exhibits 1-A to 15). Unmarked differences include: committee composition (IRS 52: "Tanaka/Andrea Reeves"; our served 40: four members; the 9/15/2016 minutes: Hargrove, Wilder, Samantha Reeves); follow-on approval date (IRS 53: 3/8/2018; ours 65: 2/28/2018); carried interest now "received by Hargrove Capital Partners LLC" (IRS 19) rather than the GP entities (ours 21) - helpful to a services theory; "sole authority" (21) and "sole discretion" (42) language; subscription-facility facts (50-51); our concessions and IC/board-minute exhibits (5-A to 5-D) dropped from the exhibit list; LPA exhibit cut to "excerpts" omitting Sections 3.3 and 5.3, Schedule A and Amendment No. 1.
- Paragraph 31 "typo correction" is not one: "Augst" appeared in our paragraph on Fund IV's final closing; IRS recasts it as the audit start date "August 5, 2019" (the MidSouth sale date), contradicting its own 26 (audit began 1/18/2021).
Action: run a machine comparison of the markup (clean version) against the 11/1 served file; demand IRS identify every changed paragraph; reserve all rights in writing before the call.

3. TIER 1 - REJECT (document-contradicted or case-critical)
(a) ClearView acquisition date (78, 83, 139: 11/8/2017 changed to 12/12/2017). Four independent sources show 11/8/2017: executed purchase agreement, closing binder, Blackpine wire, 10/25/2017 capital call. IRS cites "the executed purchase agreement" - ours is dated 11/8. Rule 91(e) makes stipulated facts conclusive, so a wrong date is dangerous. Holding period is under three years either way (965 vs. 931 days), and both dates precede enactment (12/22/2017), so the practical stake is credibility and any transition argument (note: Section 1061 applies to taxable years beginning after 12/31/2017; I see no grandfathering for pre-TCJA acquisitions, so the transition theory in the case memo is weak). Counter: demand the document IRS relies on; stipulate the exhibits and Blackpine wire; restore 11/8/2017. Paragraph 85 (IRS-drafted "Petitioners contend ... exceeds 3 years" and credit-facility theory) contradicts our own concession (2 years 7 months 22 days) - strike.
(b) GP ownership (22: 87.5% to 92.3%). Fund IV LPA Schedule A Part III, "unchanged since formation," shows Derek 87.5%, Rachel M. Hargrove (spouse) 7.5%, Hargrove Family Trust 5.0%; Part IV says Fund V mirrors it. 92.3% matches nothing (87.5+7.5=95.0). Ask for the K-1s IRS cites; an inflated percentage could support increased individual exposure. NOTE OUR ERROR: our draft (22), the case memo and the Thornfield opinion say the other 12.5% is held by investment-team professionals; IRS 23 repeats it. Correct to the LPA. This also undercuts the "shared ownership" strength in our risk assessment.
(c) GP purpose (38). IRS "primary purpose of receiving carried interest" contradicts LPA definition "General Partner Purpose" and Section 5.1 (formed to serve as general partner), and invites Section 707(a)(2)(A). Restore LPA wording, citing the LPA. Caution: the Thornfield opinion itself says GP IV has no activity apart from serving as GP "and the receipt of carried interest allocations," so avoid broader characterizations.
(d) Valuation (89-93). Reject all substituted inputs (14.8% WACC, 2.0% growth, 7.2x, $31.7M). A stipulation is for facts about what the report says, not Respondent's expert's competing opinions; these are the endpoint values of Ridgecrest's own sensitivity tables (Section 7), not "corrections." Ridgecrest's combined downside case yields EV of about $105.4M at 3/15/2018, nowhere near $31.7M. Counter: stipulate "the Ridgecrest report states ..." with 60/40 DCF/GPC weighting (IRS's "one of the approaches" is partly fair; 3.4 says DCF primary weight), with Respondent's position separately recorded as disputed. Do not concede any valuation point before expert exchange (Callahan report served 8/15/2024).
(e) Paragraph 47 ("unified investment plan" to "separate and distinct"). IRS says the plan characterization is unsupported by the documents and was approved separately. Wrong: 9/15/2016 minutes state that the initial $13.3M and anticipated $7-10M follow-on "should be viewed as components of a single, integrated investment plan," that base-case returns assumed an add-on, and resolved to reserve $7-10M over 18-24 months; LPA Section 3.3(c) aggregates initial and follow-on for returns and carry; Amendment No. 1 (3/1/2018) cites the "original investment thesis." Counter: replace labels with the objective facts (minutes content, reserve resolution, LPA 3.3(c), separate 3/2018 approval and Amendment No. 1) and keep both sides' characterizations as contentions (as in 69-70). Candidly, this theory alone does not clear Section 1061: even aggregated, the hold is about 2 years 10.5 months. Its larger value is the reasonable-cause defense and rebutting IRS's tranche math. Also note the minutes condition each deployment on future IC approval, and Ridgecrest's stated purpose (tranche-level allocation) reads against us.
(f) IC minutes deletion (62-65). Authenticity of our own business records, which IRS obtained in examination, "fairly should not be in dispute" (Rule 91(a)(1)); in any event admissible via business-records foundation (Fed. R. Evid. 803(6), 902(11), applied by Tax Court Rule 143). Counter: restore stipulation of authenticity and content; failing agreement, serve Rule 90 requests for admission (must be completed 45 days before calendar; responses due in 30 days - serve by mid-January) and prepare custodian (Marcus Leung, recording secretary) as authenticating witness.

4. TIER 2 - NEGOTIATE
- Good-faith reliance (112). IRS is partly right: "good faith" is the Court's conclusion, and Rule 91(a)(1) does not bar stipulating law-to-fact but we gain little from a contested label. Accept "received" only if IRS keeps 113-114 (reviewed, discussed, pre-filing delivery) and we add objective facts for the Neonatology prongs (Neonatology Assocs. v. Commissioner, 115 T.C. 43 (2000), aff'd, 299 F.3d 221 (3d Cir. 2002); United States v. Boyle, 469 U.S. 241 (1985); Fifth Circuit law controls under Golsen): Thornfield's competence, full information supplied, Hargrove's emails requesting the opinions and adopting the position. Before stipulating exhibits 18/19, vet: the 3/15/2020 opinion cites "Prop. Reg. 1.1061-4," yet proposed Section 1061 regulations issued 8/14/2020 (final T.D. 9945, 1/2021) - an apparent anachronism that IRS will exploit as to date/authenticity; the opinion also recites the incorrect 12.5% ownership and was written by the return preparer. Investigate with Nakamura before any stipulation of the opinions' contents (110, 116).
- Appeals statements (118 deleted). Federal Rule 408 limits settlement communications offered to prove validity of a claim, and an Appeals officer's view does not bind the Commissioner. Our served 118 also overstates the case file ("compelling," "inclined to concede"; our notes say only that she acknowledged merit). Recommend conceding deletion as a trade, with the underlying documents preserved; consider a non-hearsay use later.
- Management fee offset (152). IRS cites Section 8.3 and drops the qualifier; the offset is Section 8.2 (8.3 is organizational expenses) and applies only to the extent cumulative carry exceeds cumulative fees, with express non-recharacterization language (8.2(c)). Insert 8.2(a)-(c) verbatim and correct our own citations (our 28 also cites 8.3).
- Additions 148-158 (Section 707(a)(2)(A) record-building). The theory appeared in the 30-day letter, not clearly in the SNOD; confirm whether it is pleaded. If new matter, Respondent bears the burden (Rule 142(a)) - do not volunteer its proof. Preserve relevance objections (the preamble already allows). Specifics: 148 (65/35 time split from IDR 7 records) - verify source, reject the categories as artificial, offer "documents show"; 150 (no salary) - verify with K-1s; 151 ("no arm's-length negotiation") - reject, our 28 says the fee offset was negotiated with the advisory committee; 154 ($61.8M "enterprise" benefit) - argumentative, carry went to GP entities not HCP; 155-156 (Fund III) - accept the non-challenge fact only with years, holding periods and exit facts; 157 - correct to "no stand-alone written policy; LPA 3.3 authorizes and expects follow-ons"; 158 (3 of 11) - conflicts with our 33-34 (6 + 8 portfolio companies) - reconcile first. 153 sums correctly ($18.6M) - verify against fund financials.

5. TIER 3 - ACCEPT
Typo fixes (12, 46), date format (after comparing every date for substance), Rule 91 preamble (add "subject to relevance and materiality objections" and strike the blanket "true and correct unless objected" sentence, which preserves authenticity attacks), 159 reservation. EIN additions: acceptable but check Tax Court Rule 27 privacy treatment of identifiers, SSN digits, age and home address (our 3, IRS 14) before filing.

6. OUR OWN ERRORS TO FIX NOW (verified against the documents)
- Ridgecrest: our 86-87 say retained 1/2019, report 4/30/2019, 87 pages; the report is dated 10/15/2019, about 185 pages, marked "prepared for litigation support purposes." Our 93 values (EV $41.2M/$54.8M/$72.5M) do not match Ridgecrest (EV $80.1M/$119.7M/$158.0M; equity $68.7M/$101.5M/$135.7M); IRS's struck "$38.4M" matches neither. Our 92 calls 8.5x the median; the report says median 8.3x, selected 8.5x. Ridgecrest also says Fund IV held roughly 50% of MidSouth equity at sale and about 19.4% at entry, while we say 100% (43, 50): resolve before stipulating.
- Fund IV: committed capital $350M and closings 6/15, 9/30 and 12/15/2015 (LPA), not $225M with an "Augst 15" final closing (our 31); preferred return is non-compounded (our 27(b)); catch-up is 100% to GP (our 27(c)); sections are 7.1, 3.3 and 8.2 (we cite 7.2, 3.4, 8.3). Dates of LPA differ across documents (6/12, 6/15, 12/15/2015 restatement).
- MidSouth/ClearView headquarters and size differ across our draft, IRS draft, minutes, Ridgecrest and Thornfield; IC membership likewise. Conform to primary documents.
- IRS 28/120 wrongly say Stonebridge prepared the protest and attended Appeals; Thornfield did, and we were engaged 4/5/2023 (IRS 128 says so).
- Deficiency arithmetic reconciles ($6,579,000 + $1,470,600 + $972,000 = $9,021,600) but the $38.7M recharacterization does not match IRS's own tranche theory (about $16.8M + $10.06M = $26.9M, and with both MidSouth tranches under three years, $43.2M). Ask IRS for the computation before stipulating 68, 125. Also confirm NIIT treatment; and the memo's $935,100 "credits" explanation of Derek's lower deficiency is doubtful. Avoid IRS's "assessed" (33): the SNOD "determined." IRS 34 adds a negligence ground; check the SNOD and Section 6751(b) supervisory approval; Respondent bears the production burden for penalties (Section 7491(c)).

7. RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE
1) This week: written reply reserving rights, requesting clean/compare, the 12/12/2017 document, K-1s for 92.3%, and the IDR 7 records. 2) Before the call: fix our errors and circulate a corrected second draft built from primary documents. 3) Call 12/17-19: lead with agreed housekeeping, then documents; trade 118 for 62-65, and 112 wording for objective reliance facts. 4) Serve Rule 90 requests (authenticity of IC minutes, ClearView agreement/wire) by mid-January. 5) If impasse on 62-65, 78/83, 22, 89-93 by 1/15, file a Rule 91(f) motion with a declaration of good-faith conferral well before 2/28; IRS threatens the same, so make ours first on the document paragraphs. Do not sign any combined version.

8. UNVERIFIED
Not independently checked: Rule 27 specifics, Rule 142(a), Neonatology/Boyle/Golsen citations (from memory), whether the 707(a)(2)(A) theory is in the Answer, Fund V LPA (not supplied), actual SNOD, and the Ridgecrest 87-page versus 185-page versions. Rule 91, Rule 90 and the Section 1061 regulation dates were checked online.
